name: William Dantz
role: Little Missouri cattle rancher; Billings County officeholder
bio: William Dantz was a cattle rancher whose place lay 15 miles up the Little Missouri from Medora. In 1884 he stocked his range with Minnesota cattle, some bought for him by Daniel Friedman and brought in by Lloyd Roberts, and took part in the beef round-up that November. In October 1885 he and Alden Eaton took the first cattle shipped from Medora's new stock-yards to sell in St. Paul, and in April 1886 he unloaded 300 two-year-old heifers from Minnesota at the Medora stock yards. He ran on the Billings County and stockmen's tickets in March 1886 and won, and in October 1886 he opened the citizens' nominating convention and was again among the successful candidates.
